title: A right adjoint to an additive linear functor is additive and linear
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be $A$-linear categories [def-weil-linear-category], with their underlying preadditive structures. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be functors equipped with an ordinary adjunction $F\dashv G$, that is, natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,GY)$, and do not assume these bijections are $A$-linear. If $F$ is additive and $A$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor], then $G$ is additive and $A$-linear: for every pair of parallel morphisms $s,t$ in $\mathcal D$ and every $a\in A$, $G(s+t)=G(s)+G(t)$ and $G(as)=aG(s)$. No abelian, boundedness or exactness hypothesis on the categories or functors is imposed.

proof.text: Write $\psi_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,GY)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FX,Y)$ for the inverse of the given natural bijection, and set $\varepsilon_Y=\psi_{GY,Y}(1_{GY})$. Naturality in $X$, applied to $h:X\to GY$, gives $\psi_{X,Y}(h)=\varepsilon_Y\circ F(h)$. Naturality in $Y$, applied to $u:Y\to Z$ and $1_{GY}$, gives $\psi_{GY,Z}(G(u))=u\circ\varepsilon_Y$. These are just the two naturality squares in the hypothesis, evaluated at an identity; each $\psi_{X,Y}$ is injective because it is a bijection.

proof.text: Let $s,t:Y\to Z$ be parallel morphisms. By bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category] and additivity of $F$ [def-weil-linear-functor], the formulas of step 1 give $$\psi_{GY,Z}(G(s+t))=(s+t)\circ\varepsilon_Y=s\circ\varepsilon_Y+t\circ\varepsilon_Y=\varepsilon_Z\circ F(Gs)+\varepsilon_Z\circ F(Gt)=\varepsilon_Z\circ F(Gs+Gt)=\psi_{GY,Z}(Gs+Gt).$$ Injectivity of this same bijection proves $G(s+t)=Gs+Gt$. No additivity of $G$ or of the adjunction bijections was used.

source.place: Tags 09MJ (definition-linear-category) and 09MK (definition-functor-linear-categories); agent calculation expanding the counit proofs in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Linear/LinearFunctor.lean:27-36 and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Additive.lean:33-39.

proof.text: For $a\in A$ and $s:Y\to Z$, bilinearity of composition [def-weil-linear-category] and scalar linearity of $F$ [def-weil-linear-functor] give $$\psi_{GY,Z}(G(as))=(as)\circ\varepsilon_Y=a(s\circ\varepsilon_Y)=a(\varepsilon_Z\circ F(Gs))=\varepsilon_Z\circ(aF(Gs))=\varepsilon_Z\circ F(aGs)=\psi_{GY,Z}(aGs).$$ Injectivity proves $G(as)=aG(s)$. Together with step 2 this says precisely that the maps induced by $G$ on morphism modules are additive and $A$-linear. The argument uses only the stated natural bijections and bilinear composition, so requires no abelian, exactness or boundedness assumptions.
